notes: Site in Meridian I-20/59 Industrial Park (also called Key Brothers Industrial Park in local reporting), next to Southern Pipe and Supply. Groundbreaking ceremony Jan 2025 (WTOK 2025-01-29); groundwork June 2025; first building construction Feb 2026. $10B figure includes future tenants' IT equipment, not Compass's own spend. Tenant Corderill LLC (>= $100M equipment, >= 20 jobs, MDA approved Apr 2026) folded into this record. Local fee-in-lieu / property tax deal terms not found; CEA reports a supervisor said in Nov 2025 he had no firm fiscal projections. Acreage 303 is from Site Selection magazine, not an official record. Trackers list 320 MW; we use the company's ~500 MW. [site-numbers 2026-10-15] PSC Docket 2025-UA-25 (Halford testimony filed 2025-02-18, https://ctsportal.psc.ms.gov/portal/PSC/ViewFile?fileId=o3TkytRowWU%3D): Mississippi Power expects to start serving Compass in 2026 with load ramping to about 500 MW; only 180 MW can be served on the existing 115 kV system, so a new 230 kV switching station and lines are needed, est. $117M (2025-2032), partly offset by an up-front Compass contribution-in-aid-of-construction. CPCN approved 2025-05-01. This corroborates the company's 500 MW. MDEQ Air Construction Permit 1460-00133 (Compass Datacenters JAN I, LLC, I20-59 Industrial Park; issued 2026-06-24; AI 87959) covers 10 buildings, each with 42 emergency diesel generators (40 x 2,000 kW Caterpillar 3516C, 1 x 800 kW, 1 x 500 kW): 420 generators, about 813 MW of backup capacity (our math; backup, not grid load). Lauderdale County's own MDEQ stormwater NOI for 'I-20/59 Industrial Park Phase II' (AI 87168; 276 total project acres; entrance 32 deg 23' 25" N, 88 deg 37' 16" W) is for the park, not the Compass parcel, so it is not used as the pin. official_statements.text: Greenidge 8-K: Greenidge Mississippi LLC agreed to sell an approximately 6.4 acre parcel at 249 Datco Industrial Road, Columbus, Mississippi 39707, with the site's mining equipment (no bitcoin miners), to US Digital Mining Mississippi LLC for about $3.9 million. Excluded: about 73,000 sq ft of warehouse space on an adjoining tract bought in March 2024.

LM Funding America closed the acquisition of an 11 MW bitcoin mining site in Columbus, Mississippi from Greenidge Generation Holdings for $4.0 million total, including about 7.5 MW (157 PH/s) of operating miners (about 2,300 Bitmain S19s); power about $0.036/kWh.

LM Funding 10-K: as of December 31, 2025 the company owned an 11 MW hosting site in Columbus, Mississippi with about 2,380 installed S19 or S19J Pro Antminer machines (projected hashrate 238 PH); 'We own approximately six acres in Columbus, Mississippi.'

Todd Liebel, VP of the operating company: the site shuts down during daily peak hours ('when the load starts getting a little hot... we turn off'), Columbus Light and Water offered it off-peak power, and four on-site technicians run the site (as reported).

PowerCompute (Nasdaq: PWCM, formerly LM Funding America): subsidiary US Digital Mining Mississippi LLC signed a contract with Columbus Light and Water on 2026-09-30 raising contracted demand from 8.5 MW to 11 MW, effective October 1, 2026, on the Large Data Service Rate (Schedule DCB) that implements TVA's new data center rate; no TVA capacity commitment charge assessed; the utility is returning a $300,000 deposit (replaced by a bond); about 2,373 installed Antminers, about 205 PH/s as of 2026-09-30.

PowerCompute 8-K: the new Industrial Power Contract supplies up to 11,000 kW of firm power to the 'data center in Columbus, Mississippi', runs to 2030-09-16 with a possible five-year renewal, and the company's share of the utility's capital costs is estimated at $0.
PowerCompute: generated about $89,000 in September 2026 and about $312,000 in Q3 2026 by selling energy during heat-related curtailment at its Oklahoma and Mississippi sites.
Greenidge's 12-acre Mississippi mining site began operating July 1, 2024 with 8.5 MW of power; Greenidge planned to secure an additional 25 MW within the next year (as reported).

notes: Bitcoin mining site at 249 Datco Industrial Road, Columbus (Lowndes County), per Greenidge's 8-K (2025-08-06) and LM Funding's 10-K (2026-03-31). History: Greenidge bought about 12 acres with over 73,000 sq ft of warehouse in Columbus in April 2024 (Greenidge 10-K, filed 2026-03-31) and started mining there July 1, 2024 at 8.5 MW (Oxford Eagle). Greenidge sold the 6.4-acre mining parcel to US Digital Mining Mississippi LLC (LM Funding subsidiary), closing 2025-09-16 for about $3.9M, and kept the adjoining 5.6-acre warehouse tract; LM Funding reported $4.0M total including miners. That explains the old acreage conflict (Oxford Eagle 12 acres = whole Greenidge purchase; The Block 6.4 acres = the parcel sold), so acres is now 6.4 from the SEC filing. LM Funding renamed itself PowerCompute (Nasdaq: PWCM). Power: old power_mw value (11 MW contracted, source finviz copy of the 2026-10-06 release) is now sourced to the filed contract (8-K Exhibit 10.1). The contract allows only 300 kW on-peak; the site curtails at peak and sells power back in hot months. The 8-K says the contract was signed 2026-09-30 'but effective as of September 16, 2026'; the press release says it took effect October 1, 2026. Tier small: 11 MW is below the ~20 MW / $100M line. Purchase price is an acquisition price, not build investment, so investment_usd null. jobs_actual 4 is the company VP's count as told to The Dispatch (2026-05-30); the 10-K says about nine staff were added across the Oklahoma and Mississippi sites in 2025. lat/lng left null: the street address is official, but no permit, plat or official map with coordinates was found. TVA's Large Data Service rate (adopted Aug 2026) counts bitcoin mining as data center load. Columbus Light and Water is a TVA distributor, so its rates are set under TVA, not the Mississippi PSC. No MDEQ permit, tax break, community deal, or local government vote for this site was found. Separate Greenidge project: Greenidge's 10-K says it owns a 34-acre greenfield site in Columbus expecting 40 MW by Q1 2027 (and its Q1 2026 results mention a 250 MW load study); that is NOT this site.

Pearl River County: population 57,458 vs 57,838 (-1%), median household income $58,135 vs $53,812 (+8%). Pearl River is also the comparison county for Warren County; it borders Stone County, home of the small CleanSpark Wiggins bitcoin site (the Mississippi rule does not exclude that). Caution: Lowndes has far more jobs located in the county than Pearl River (26,162 vs 11,726 in 2025) and a higher average weekly wage ($1,140 vs $820), BLS QCEW, so compare changes, not levels.
